channel.title: [podly] The AI Daily Brief: Artificial Intelligence News and Analysis
channel.description: A daily news analysis show on all things artificial intelligence. NLW looks at AI from multiple angles, from the explosion of creativity brought on by new tools like Midjourney and ChatGPT to the potential disruptions to work and industries as we know them to the great philosophical, ethical and practical questions of advanced general intelligence, alignment and x-risk.

item.title: Washington Is Taking Control of AI
item.ns0:encoded:
Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia is becoming a turning point in Washington’s battle over AI and China. NLW examines how the fallout is empowering China hawks, accelerating chip export restrictions, and raising questions that go well beyond the disputed spy allegations. Plus, the competing arguments over selling chips to China—and what new leadership at Nvidia could mean for the financing that keeps the AI boom moving.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Out. Everything in AI Is Now Up for Grabs.
item.ns0:encoded:
Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia, leaving a power vacuum that stretches across the AI industry. NLW examines the allegations behind his departure, who stands to benefit, and what happens when the industry loses one of its most influential figures. From China policy and open source to the financial commitments supporting the AI buildout, the consequences go far beyond Nvidia.

item.title: Wall Street Has No Idea What Anthropic Is Worth
item.ns0:encoded:
Anthropic is heading into its IPO with surging revenue, massive compute commitments, and a new productivity suite taking aim at Microsoft. NLW breaks down the competing bull and bear cases, why the valuation headlines are misleading, and what the offering could mean for the entire AI trade. In the headlines: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, Nvidia’s China scandal deepens, and OpenAI’s revenue surges.

item.title: Fable 5.2 Is the Best AI Ever. So Why Am I Not Switching Yet?
item.ns0:encoded:
Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 is breaking benchmarks and powering ambitious demos, so why isn’t it an obvious upgrade for everyday work? NLW examines early reviews and his own experiments to explore where the model outperforms Opus 5.5, where it still falls short, and why its biggest opportunities may require rethinking what we ask AI to do.

item.title: Agentic Video Is Real and Here’s What You Should Try
item.ns0:encoded:
AI agents are making it possible to edit, animate, and produce videos simply by describing what you want. NLW explores what changed and how to put it to work—from meeting highlights and concept demos to animated business updates and customer education videos that update themselves. Plus, three levels for getting started, from editing existing recordings to building recurring video workflows.

item.title: Companies Are Spending 5x More on AI Now
item.ns0:encoded:
Companies are spending nearly five times more on AI than last year, and agents are driving the surge. NLW breaks down Menlo Ventures’ latest enterprise AI report, exploring why spending is blowing past budgets, how Anthropic and OpenAI are capturing the market, and what the shift from seats to tokens means for businesses. In the headlines: a massive market selloff, uncertainty around Anthropic’s IPO, and METR’s report on AI accelerating AI research.
